vignette: Raj, a 35-year-old South Asian male and tax consultant, has recently returned from his voluntary stint as a relief worker in a war-torn region. Now married with a young child on the way, Raj's life seems to have fallen into disarray since he returned home six months ago. In the war zone, Raj experienced countless harrowing events. He remembers vividly the night when mortar fire lit up the sky, forcing him and his team to seek shelter in an underground bunker for hours. The constant threat of violence, the sight of injured civilians, and the sounds of distant gunfire have left indelible marks on his psyche. Back home, Raj finds himself haunted by these memories. At night, he is often roused from sleep by nightmares where he relives those moments of intense fear and helplessness. In one recurring dream, he's trapped in that bunker, listening to the explosions grow closer with no escape. When he wakes up drenched in sweat, his heart racing, Raj has to remind himself he's safe. During the day, his mind often drifts back to the war zone, particularly when he hears loud noises or sees news coverage of conflict. A sudden bang from a car backfiring on his drive home can send him into a panic, and he finds it hard to focus at work because of intrusive thoughts about the traumatic events. As a tax consultant, Raj's job requires intense concentration and attention to detail. Lately, however, he struggles to maintain this level of focus. His mind wanders frequently, and he often makes simple mistakes that he would usually catch immediately. His colleagues have noticed his distraction but haven't yet commented on it directly. He feels a growing sense of incompetence and shame about his faltering performance. Raj's wife, Priya, has also observed changes in him. She describes him as more distant, less engaged in their conversations. On the rare occasions when they do discuss his experiences, Raj can feel himself shutting down emotionally, almost as if he's protecting himself from further pain. He knows that talking about it might help but feels overwhelmed by the intensity of those memories. Raj has also become increasingly irritable and anxious around crowded places. This became particularly apparent during a recent visit to their local grocery store. The sound of children playing near the checkout line triggered a panic attack, causing him to flee the store and head home immediately. Since then, he avoids such public spaces as much as possible. In his daily life, Raj finds himself hyper-vigilant, constantly on edge. He checks the locks on their doors multiple times a day and keeps the news volume low even when it's turned off in case of sudden alerts or announcements that could startle him. Despite these struggles, Raj remains committed to Priya and their upcoming child. He knows his condition is affecting his ability to be present for her and anticipates the challenges he might face as a parent. The thought of passing on any form of fear or anxiety to his child weighs heavily on him. As Raj navigates this new reality, he feels isolated and unsure how to manage these overwhelming symptoms. His once orderly life seems to have spiraled out of control, leaving him grappling with the specter of war that continues to haunt him even in the safety of his home.
